title: Sidewall Metrology Protocol for Superconducting Qubit Devices
authors: Jørgen Garnæs, Henrik S. Guttesen, Astrid T. Rømer, Oscar Danielsson, Emily P. Duggan, Zhenhai Sun, Asen Lyubenov Georgiev, Li Wei Chang, Morten Kjaergaard, Mark Bieler, Lukas Grünhaupt, Sabbir A. Khan
abstract: Sidewall morphology is a potentially important factor influencing superconducting qubit performance, yet its quantitative characterization remains challenging due to the absence of standardized measurement protocols. In this work, we develop a scanning probe microscopy-based measurement framework for the quantitative characterization of superconducting qubit sidewalls. The framework introduces a refined root mean square lateral sidewall roughness descriptor and a new curvature-equivalent radius for quantifying vertical sidewall morphology. The descriptors and measurement procedures are applied to different components of qubit devices, forming the basis of a proposed sidewall characterization protocol. This provides a foundation for quantitative comparisons of fabrication processes across laboratories, enabling future investigations of correlations between sidewall geometry and qubit performance.
summary: This work establishes a quantitative, standardized protocol for measuring sidewall morphology in superconducting qubit devices using advanced scanning probe microscopy. By introducing new descriptors for roughness and curvature, the authors provide a foundation for comparing fabrication processes across different labs. This research links nanoscale geometry directly to potential sources of energy loss in quantum circuits.
main_problem: Quantitatively characterizing sidewall morphology in superconducting qubit devices is challenging due to the lack of standardized measurement protocols, despite sidewall geometry potentially affecting qubit performance.
main_result: The authors developed a comprehensive scanning probe microscopy framework introducing new quantitative descriptors like refined RMS lateral roughness and curvature-equivalent radius for standardized sidewall characterization.
method: The study uses Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) with specialized configurations (tilted/3D) to measure sidewall profiles, developing specific protocols for data processing and artifact mitigation.
model_or_system: The physical system is superconducting qubit devices (e.g., Transmon qubits) and their associated Josephson junctions and resonators, where sidewall profiles are critical interfaces.
key_observables: Refined root mean square lateral sidewall roughness descriptor (RLSP_q), curvature-equivalent radius (Rρ), and minimum radius of curvature (ρ_min).
important_parameters: Dielectric loss ($ rac{1}{T_{	ext{dielectric}}}$), electric field concentration, and the scale of roughness (e.g., 2-5 nm to 30 nm).
main_assumptions: The measured roughness is proposed as a *proxy* for underlying material/interface properties, not a direct measure of superconducting quality, and no universal monotonic relation to quality factors is expected.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the qubit blueprint, schematics for AFM measurement approaches (tilted/vertical profiles), and detailed analysis of sidewall profiles showing measured roughness and radii of curvature.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the measurement gap to developing the quantitative descriptors (RLSP_q, Rρ), detailing the measurement procedures (AFM setup, probe correction), and finally discussing the implications for qubit loss mechanisms and measurement variability.
why_interesting: While highly experimental, the focus on quantifying material interfaces and loss mechanisms in superconducting circuits directly impacts the coherence time ($T_1$) of qubits, which is central to quantum computation.
